fields.name: memory_limit
fields.label: Memory limit
fields.help: Optional. The most memory this app's own container may use. Left empty it gets 1g, which is what this app has been measured to need — set it lower and the app may not start, and it will fail as a 502 with nothing about memory to explain it. Any database this app brings has its own separate ceiling.

fields.name: cpu_limit
fields.label: CPU limit
fields.help: Optional. How many CPU cores this app's own container may use — 1 for one full core, 0.5 for half. This server has 4, and Docker will not start a container asking for more. Left empty there is no CPU limit at all. Going past this does not kill anything; the container waits, so the symptom is slowness rather than an error. Any database this app brings is not limited by it.

starter_files./ps-init/start.sh:
#!/bin/sh
# Managed by the panel's PrestaShop recipe (RC-37). The container runs this
# before the image's own /tmp/docker_run.sh.
root=/var/www/html

# HTTPS behind the panel's proxy: PHP sees HTTPS=on for requests the proxy
# received over HTTPS (PrestaShop's secure-mode check and the Symfony back
# office both read it).
echo 'SetEnvIf X-Forwarded-Proto https HTTPS=on' > /etc/apache2/conf-enabled/zz-forwarded-https.conf

if [ -f "$root/app/config/parameters.php" ]; then
    # Installed, or an installation that stopped half-way (the image then
    # takes its "already installed" path and would serve the web installer
    # to anyone). A completed setup removes both install.lock and the
    # installer folder, so either one still being there means the last
    # installation never finished: remove the installer so it is not public.
    if [ -e "$root/install.lock" ] || [ -d "$root/$PS_FOLDER_INSTALL" ]; then
        echo "[ps-init] the PrestaShop installation did not finish (see the first start's log); the web installer was removed so it is not public. Delete and recreate the app to install again."
        rm -rf "${root:?}/${PS_FOLDER_INSTALL:?}"
    fi
    # Drop the installation-time alias (below) and follow a domain change.
    if [ -L "$root/admin-dev" ]; then
        rm -f "$root/admin-dev"
    fi
    if [ -f /ps-init/sync-domain.php ]; then
        # The database may still be starting (a restart restarts it too):
        # wait for it, up to about two minutes, with the password in the
        # environment rather than on a command line. --connect-timeout keeps
        # each try short: Docker's DNS fails for a stopped container and the
        # client would otherwise retry for its 12-hour default. The script itself runs
        # with exception arguments and error display off, so a failure can
        # never print a connection string with the password into the log.
        n=0
        until MYSQL_PWD="$DB_PASSWD" mysqladmin --connect-timeout=2 ping -h "$DB_SERVER" -P "$DB_PORT" -u "$DB_USER" --silent >/dev/null 2>&1 || [ "$n" -ge 60 ]; do
            n=$((n + 1))
            sleep 2
        done
        runuser -u www-data -- php -d zend.exception_ignore_args=1 -d display_errors=0 -d log_errors=0 /ps-init/sync-domain.php || true
    fi
elif [ ! -e "$root/admin-dev" ]; then
    # PrestaShop 9.2's installer installs the back-office assets into admin/,
    # or into admin-dev/ when admin/ is gone. The image has already renamed
    # admin/ to PS_FOLDER_ADMIN by then, so the install died on a missing
    # admin-dev/ and left the web installer public (RC-37 smoke). Point
    # admin-dev at the real folder for the installation, and remove the alias
    # as soon as the image reports the setup completed.
    ln -s "$PS_FOLDER_ADMIN" "$root/admin-dev"
    (
        n=0
        until [ -f "$root/app/config/parameters.php" ] && [ ! -e "$root/install.lock" ]; do
            n=$((n + 1))
            [ "$n" -ge 360 ] && exit 0
            sleep 5
        done
        rm -f "$root/admin-dev"
    ) &
fi

exec /tmp/docker_run.sh
starter_files./ps-init/sync-domain.php:
<?php

// Managed by the panel's PrestaShop recipe (RC-37). Run by the container's start
// command, as www-data, before Apache starts on an installed shop.
//
// PrestaShop keeps its domain in the database. The panel passes the site's
// current domain as PS_DOMAIN, so after a domain change this moves the main shop
// URL to it and regenerates what depends on it, the same steps as the image's
// own docker_updt_ps_domains.php. Nothing happens when they already match.
// Delete this file to manage the domain yourself (Shop Parameters > Traffic & SEO).

$domain = strtolower((string) getenv('PS_DOMAIN'));
if (! preg_match('/^[a-z0-9]([a-z0-9.-]*[a-z0-9])?$/', $domain)) {
    exit(0);
}

ini_set('display_errors', '0');
ini_set('zend.exception_ignore_args', '1');

$_SERVER['HTTP_HOST'] = $domain;
$_SERVER['SERVER_NAME'] = $domain;
$_SERVER['REQUEST_METHOD'] = 'GET';
$_SERVER['REQUEST_URI'] = '/';
chdir('/var/www/html');

try {
    require '/var/www/html/config/config.inc.php';
    sync_domain($domain);
} catch (Throwable $e) {
    // Only the class name: messages and traces can carry the database DSN.
    echo 'sync-domain: skipped ('.get_class($e).")\n";
}

function sync_domain(string $domain): void
{
    if (Shop::isFeatureActive()) {
        echo "sync-domain: multistore is on, domains are left alone\n";

        return;
    }

    if (Configuration::get('PS_SHOP_DOMAIN') === $domain && Configuration::get('PS_SHOP_DOMAIN_SSL') === $domain) {
        return;
    }

    $url = ShopUrl::getShopUrls((int) Configuration::get('PS_SHOP_DEFAULT'))->where('main', '=', 1)->getFirst();
    if ($url) {
        $url->domain = $domain;
        $url->domain_ssl = $domain;
        $url->save();
    }

    Configuration::updateValue('PS_SHOP_DOMAIN', $domain);
    Configuration::updateValue('PS_SHOP_DOMAIN_SSL', $domain);
    Tools::generateHtaccess();
    Tools::generateRobotsFile();
    Tools::clearSmartyCache();
    Media::clearCache();
    Tools::clearSf2Cache();

    echo "sync-domain: shop domain set to {$domain}\n";
}
